fullPassage:
(A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

(B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

(C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!

❌ ① bore(지루하게 하다): amuse의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ② entertain(즐겁게 하다): amuse와 동의어. Emma가 자기 자신을 즐겁게 하려고(amuse herself) 방해 행동을 했다
❌ ③ irritate(짜증나게 하다): amuse와 반대 의미
❌ ④ discipline(훈육하다): '자기 자신을 즐겁게 하다'와 의미 불일치
det.tip: amuse = entertain = 즐겁게 하다. amuse oneself = 스스로를 즐겁게 하다

questions.passage:
Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>suggesting</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① demanding(요구하는): suggesting의 의미보다 훨씬 강한 어감
❌ ② rejecting(거부하는): suggesting과 의미 불일치
❌ ③ concealing(숨기는): suggesting과 반대 의미
✅ ④ indicating(나타내는): suggesting과 동의어. 연구가 ~을 시사했다(research suggesting ~)
det.tip: suggesting = indicating = 시사하는, 나타내는. research suggesting ~ = 연구가 ~을 시사하는

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>enable</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① allow(허용하다): enable과 유사한 의미로 반의어 아님
✅ ② prevent(막다): enable(가능하게 하다)의 반의어. 학교가 비상 상태에서 벗어나게 하는 것(enable)을 막는 것(prevent)
❌ ③ assist(돕다): enable과 유사한 의미로 반의어 아님
❌ ④ facilitate(촉진하다): enable과 유사한 의미로 반의어 아님
det.tip: enable(가능하게 하다) ↔ prevent(막다, 방지하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>newfound</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: newfound = 새로 발견한, 새로운 ↔ established = 확립된, 오래된
det.analysis:
✅ ① established(확립된, 오래된): newfound(새로 발견한, 새로운)의 반의어. 이미 오래 확립된 것
❌ ② recent(최근의): newfound와 유사한 의미
❌ ③ fresh(신선한, 새로운): newfound와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ novel(새로운): newfound와 유사한 의미
det.tip: newfound(새로 발견한) ↔ established(확립된, 기존의). Emma의 새로운 자신감(newfound confidence)

questions.passage:
(A) The teacher tried to <u>sound out</u> each student's opinion on the topic. She asked questions one by one to understand their perspectives.

(B) Sandy wanted Emma to <u>sound out</u> every word carefully. With practice, Emma's ability to read aloud improved significantly.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문맥에서 밑줄 친 sound out의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? (A) The teacher tried to sound out each student's opinion on the topic. (B) Sandy wanted Emma to sound out every word carefully.

det.korean: sound out: (A) 의견을 탐색하다 (B) 단어를 소리 내어 읽다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 목소리를 높이다: (A)의 의미 불일치
❌ ② (A) 소리를 측정하다: (A)의 의미 불일치
✅ ③ (A) 의견을 탐색하다 (B) 단어를 소리 내어 읽다: (A) sound out = 의견을 탐색하다(떠보다). (B) sound out = 소리 내어 읽다(음독). 본문에서 Emma의 음독 능력 향상이 핵심
❌ ④ (B) 단어를 암기하다: (B)의 의미 불일치. sound out은 암기가 아닌 소리 내어 읽기
det.tip: sound out: (1) 의견/반응을 탐색하다 (2) (글자를) 소리 내어 읽다. 본문은 (2)의 의미

ch: (A) 소리를 측정하다 (B) 단어를 소리 내어 읽다
(A) 의견을 탐색하다 (B) 단어를 소리 내어 읽다

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to go upward; to move to a higher position or level"

det.korean: 위로 올라가다; 더 높은 위치나 수준으로 이동하다 = ascend(오르다, 상승하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① descend(내려가다): 반의어
✅ ② ascend(오르다, 상승하다): go upward, move to a higher position. 본문의 'help enable her school to ascend from its academic emergency status'
❌ ③ collapse(무너지다): 반의어
❌ ④ remain(남아 있다): 위치 이동 없음
det.tip: ascend = 오르다, 상승하다. to go upward or to a higher level

questions.passage: Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming __________ (disrupt) or feeling anxious.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로) (1단어)

det.analysis: without becoming __________(disrupt)에서 becoming 뒤에는 보어 역할의 형용사가 필요. disrupt(동사) → disruptive(형용사: 방해가 되는). become + 형용사 구문.
det.tip: disrupt(동사: 방해하다) → disruptive(형용사: 방해가 되는). become + 형용사 보어

questions.passage: Sandy __________ (recall) research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로) (1단어)

det.analysis: Sandy __________(recall)에서 문장의 시제가 과거(That evening after school, Sandy reflected...)이므로 recall → recalled. 과거 시제 일치.
det.tip: recall(회상하다) → recalled(과거형). 전체 서사가 과거 시제

det.korean: 빈칸: 새로 얻게 된 자신감(newfound confidence)
det.analysis:
❌ ① persistent frustration(지속적인 좌절감): Emma가 좌절로 인해 다른 책을 읽고 싶어졌다는 것은 문맥에 부적절

det.tip: newfound confidence = 새로 얻게 된 자신감. Emma의 성장의 결과
